_doc: Coefficients of the tile route graph (sim/geography/routes_graph.py and routes_rates.py). Mode physics lives in ../route_modes/.

entries.source: Same value the economy's tile freight graph uses; research notes put unbuilt tracks at 1.25 to 1.4 circuity.
entries.why: Tracks wind around hills, rivers and marsh; tiles carry no road network, so a flat factor stands in until relief derives it.

entries.source: Meander ratios of navigable rivers, 1.4 to 2.0 in the research notes (low end kept: tile centres sit near the main stem).
entries.why: A boat follows the channel, not the chord between tile centres.

entries.source: Same value as the economy's sea detour; coastal circuity 1.2 to 1.5 in the research notes.
entries.why: Coastal shipping follows the shore and puts in at headlands; tiles carry no coastline.

entries.source: Open-sea circuity about 1.05 to 1.1 in the research notes.
entries.why: A hull crossing open water holds close to the chord.

entries.source: Same range as the economy's sea links.
entries.why: Coastal tiles within this range are one coast-hugging leg apart; longer voyages chain legs.

entries.source: Blue-water crossings of one to two thousand km in the research notes.
entries.why: Coastal tiles farther apart than the coast range but within this one are joined by an open-sea leg, which a sea lane may restrict.

entries.source: Pre-compass pilots kept land in sight or crossed short gaps; a day's sail is about 100 km.
entries.why: A catalogue sea link whose water path never strays farther than this from a coast is a coast leg, else an open-sea leg a lane may restrict.

entries.source: About two thirds of the radius of an equal-area tile cell.
entries.why: A sea leg whose chord passes this close to another tile's centre is taken to cross land and is dropped, since tiles carry no land mask.

entries.source: Mean sustained grade of overland tracks across mixed country; no relief layer was available.
entries.why: Used for a land edge when neither tile has an elevation or ruggedness layer.

entries.unit: grade per metre of in-tile elevation standard deviation
entries.source: Research notes section 2: climbs follow passes, not tile means, so grade is taken from in-tile relief.
entries.why: Turns the elevation_std_m layer into the grade a path must climb.

entries.source: ruggedness_index is the mean absolute height difference to neighbouring DEM cells; real tracks climb steeper than the cell-to-cell slope, so it is scaled to match the elevation_std_m rule on typical tiles.
entries.why: Turns the ruggedness_index layer into a grade when a tile has no elevation_std_m.
Bounds the grade an edge can carry whatever the layers say.

entries.source: Research notes section 6: navigability needs a draught-deep reach.
entries.why: A river edge joins bordering tiles that both carry at least this much navigable river.

entries.unit: labour-hours per kg of feed grain
entries.source: Pre-industrial grain output of about a tonne per farmer-year.
entries.why: Lets a carrier's feed be added to its crew hours when the caller supplies no prices.

entries.source: Hand-hewn coal output of a few hundred kg a shift.
entries.why: Lets a steam carrier's fuel be added to its crew hours when the caller supplies no prices.

entries.source: Research notes section 3: wagons on unpaved tracks make 15 to 20 km a day against 25 to 35 on a good road.
entries.why: Ruts and mud slow carts on an unbuilt track; a built road restores the full pace.
